The tick is the composition root: pass() orders every step that moves without a command (idle, lines, bumps, worker health, one admitted start, resume, watch look, swap), and each step's rules already live behind deeper modules (line.rs via lines(), load.rs, swap.rs, issues.rs blockers, domain admission/bump/worker). Its interface is small: tick/run/stop/daemon_start, and scenarios test through tick() only. Churn is features adding one step each, which belong in the pass's order here; daemon.rs was already deepened by factorium#93 (lines) and #134 (swap). Moving bumps/next_issue/resume_parked out would only relocate one-call private helpers, not add depth.

Deep already: callers (gate.rs, line/cut.rs, idle.rs, daemon.rs) use one entry, heavy(Job, Turn), plus Job's per-kind constructors and the tick hooks asking_once/beside/adopt_queued/note_rules; behind it sit queueing, place-keeping, stale-rules exec, dead-pid cleanup, session noting, hold-bound and give-way ending. Deletion test: removing it would spread that protocol over its four callers. Rules already live in factorium_domain::heavy; no unit tests reach past the interface (covered by queue/admission scenarios). Churn is feature work on the queue (factorium#193/#194), not interface friction. factorium#206

Size is ~20 one-rule commands plus wait() and Decided placement, each needing Issue's state; splitting waits or numbering out would move code and widen the interface (Issue internals pub) without concentrating anything. Tests go through the public functions only.

Deep already: one input record (Seen) and three pure functions (findings, unstarted, no_daemon) hide every finding's rule, key, wording and fix; callers in the effect crate and tests (scenarios/stall.rs, admission.rs) only cross that interface. Its churn is each new finding added in its one home, which is the locality the module exists for; splitting it by finding would spread one concept over many shallow modules with the same interface.
